sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR DISMISSAL, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The above appeal is filed by the Claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 28.3.2013 passed in MVC No.2982/2011 by the Judge, Court of Small Causes, 26th ACMM, Bangalore1 wherein, the Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition filed by the claimant.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred as per their rank before the Tribunal.
3.

entities.text: Court of Small Causes, 26th ACMM, Bangalore1
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The relevant facts necessary for consideration of the above appeal are that the appellant-claimant filed a claim petition claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident alleged to have occurred on 22.4.2011.

It is the case of the claimant that while walking on the left side of the road, the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-02/EQ.4033 came in a rash and negligent Hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal' NC: 2024:KHC:2266 manner and hit her causing the accident in question wherein, she suffered grievous injuries.

Claiming compensation for the same,
the claim petition was filed arraying the insurer and owner of the motor cycle as respondents.
The insurer entered appearance before the Tribunal and contested the case.
The owner remained ex parte.
The claimant examined herself as PW.1 and a doctor as PW.2
Exs.P1 to P14 were marked in evidence.
The official of the insurer was examined as RW.1.
Exs.R1 and 2 were marked in evidence.
The Tribunal by its judgment and award dated 28.3.2013 dismissed the claim petition.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal is filed.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant vehemently contended that the Tribunal has erroneously disbelieved that the accident in question was caused due to the negligent act of the rider of the motor cycle and in view of the fact that the charge sheet has been filed by the police authorities which has not been challenged, the Tribunal ought not to have dismissed the claim petition.

Further,
it is contended that the complainant adequately explained the delay in filing NC: 2024:KHC:2266 the complaint and the fact that the claimant has sustained grievous injuries not having been disputed, the Tribunal ought to have awarded adequate compensation.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the first respondent - insurer justifies the award passed by the Tribunal and seeks for dismissal of the above appeal.

sentences.text: The submissions of both the learned counsel have been considered and the material on record including the records of the Tribunal have been perused.
The question that arises for consideration is, whether the finding of the Tribunal dismissing the claim petition is erroneous and liable to be interfered with?

7. The Tribunal noticed the MLC register of Saptagiri Hospital, Bangalore (Ex.R2) wherein, it is forthcoming in the column for history of the accident that it has been mentioned as a road traffic accident of a bike who hit and ran away.
That the said entry clearly discloses that the accident was a hit and run case.
The Tribunal further noticed the cross- examination of PW.1 wherein, she has stated that the motor cycle fell down after hitting her and she has seen its number.
NC: 2024:KHC:2266 That the claimant is an educated lady having completed her post graduation at Bengaluru University, ought to have mentioned the number in the complaint itself.
Not having done so, the Tribunal has recorded a finding that an unknown vehicle hit the claimant and went away.
The Tribunal has also noticed the fact that the claimant has not at all given a statement to the concerned police.

8. Further, the Tribunal noticed that the complaint and FIR (Ex.P1) was lodged after a lapse of 8 days from the date of the accident and with respect to delay in lodging the complaint, the complainant has stated that the rider of the motor cycle assured her that he will bear all the medical expenses and by saying the same he went away, but failed to return back and thereafter, she lodged the complaint.

However, it was further noticed that since the claimant had herself seen the registration number of the motor cycle after the accident, if the rider of the motor cycle failed to return back after a lapse of 2 or 3 days, she ought to have lodged the complaint, which she has not done so.
Further, it is noticed that the claimant has not examined any eye witness.

The Tribunal noticing the various inconsistencies in the case of the claimant, has recorded a finding that the same creates a doubt in the mind of the Court to believe the case of the claimant and the trustworthiness of PW.1 and hence, held that the claimant is unable to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the motor cycle.
10. Upon a re-appreciation of the aforementioned, it is clear that in Ex.R2 i.e., MLC register, it is mentioned as "H/o RTA rider hit her and ray away, no clues about the rider".
Further, the complaint is lodged after 8 days from the date of the accident.
That PW.1 has admitted that she has seen the number of the motor cycle when the accident occurred.
The claimant is admittedly an educated lady.

Hence, at the first instance, in Ex.R2 it having been recorded that there is no clue about the rider and as noticed by the Tribunal the delay in lodging the complaint and FIR is also not satisfactorily explained, the appellant has failed in demonstrating that the findings recorded by the Tribunal are in any manner erroneous having been recorded contrary to NC: 2024:KHC:2266 the material available on record and that the said findings liable to be interfered with by this Court in the present appeal.
Hence the question framed for consideration is answered in the negative.
